prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation; transformer/feeder bays. Supervisory, bay execution and protection comms layers are separate; no silent substitution. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): sequencing/interlocks; executes only approved-logic/interlock-permitted commands; validates requests (mode, interlocks, authority, availability); flags bad operations; links Breaker Inspection Tag to records; marks stale points degraded; sends Bay Status Digest to Glasswing; receives Battery Load Test Record. North/South Bay Controllers: block close without interlocks; North keeps local control in supervisory loss; South reports local mode. Breaker Control Unit: executes accepted commands, rejects non-permissive ones; returns position/health; local interlocks authoritative; tests cannot bypass. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): protection independent of supervisory comms; sends Relay Diagnostic Note to Larkspur; tests keep energized-feeder coverage. North Protection Panel: network-independent trips. Transformer Protection Panel: reports abnormal conditions. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): no protection; shows indications, command results, quality/stale; retains alarms; Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; receives Protocol Retry Summary. Station Gateway: sole external boundary; rejects/logs bad requests; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): sends Clock Drift Snapshot to Orchard; time-quality issues investigated before sequence analysis. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative time-ordered events. Engineering Workstation: authorized config under change control; sends Settings Review Receipt to Maintenance Remote Terminal. Station DC System: produces Battery Load Test Record; confirmed available before control-power-dependent switching. Actors: Control Room Operator: decides request appropriateness; requests to Keystone; sends Clearance Handoff Memo to Keystone (checks vs switching record); tracks out-of-service protection; confirms indications locally if remote incomplete/delayed. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings, test scope, restoration; reviews after changes; assesses unexplained trips before return. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): Breaker Inspection Tag; uses Isolation Boundary Card to verify boundary; works after clearance/isolation/grounding; reports issues, pauses if boundary uncertain. Substation Supervisor: change control; before normal service confirms records, cleared restrictions, risk owners. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): prerequisites/sequence, Isolation Boundary Card, handback; confirms authority/state/comms limits before automation actions. Rules: remote commands inhibited if status uncertain; manual operation by procedure; faults assessed before restart/bypass/replacement; restoration confirms indications, protection,

Document units:

S241: The North Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S242: The South Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
S243: The North Protection Panel shall remain available for independent protection functions during supervisory control interruptions.
S244: The Transformer Protection Panel shall remain within its approved settings and operating constraints during handover.
S245: Periodic operational reviews shall examine command outcomes, event records, exceptions, and corrective actions so that automation decisions remain traceable and safe.
